newsitem.title: USA: Emisphere pact seen as a milestone.
newsitem.headline: Emisphere pact seen as a milestone.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co's agreement to use Emisphere Technologies Inc's drug delivery technology could ultimately prove to be a windfall for Emisphere if it fared well in clinical trials.
On Thursday, Emisphere and Lilly said they had entered into a strategic alliance worth up to $60 million in payments to Emisphere.
"It's a very important milestone for the company," said David Steinberg, an analyst with Volpe, Welty & Co.
The pact focuses on the oral delivery of protein treatments for endocrinological conditions, including growth disorders.
In December, Emisphere reported a first quarter loss of $0.11 a share on revenues of $1.99 million, compared with a loss of $0.25 a share on no revenues the previous first quarter.

Emisphere stock closed down 1/2 at 23-3/4 Thursday, after having traded at a new high of 27-1/2 earlier in the day. Lilly stock closed down four points at 87-3/4, along with the rest of the drug stock group, which suffered similar declines.
"If the money is realized, that's very significant. It would provide cash inflow to Emisphere to support some of its important programs," Steinberg said.
Steinberg cautions that since the products are in early testing stages, there is the clinical trial risk for them.
Michael Goldberg, Emisphere's chairman and chief executive officer, told Reuters that he expects to start clinical trials within a year for at least one product from the alliance.
